description: Structural contract for Perry state files. The single source of truth that SKILL.md prose, state/*_TEMPLATE.md, and viewer/parsers.py must all agree with. Validated by bin/perry-lint (against a project) and by tests/ (against the templates themselves).

work_modes.note: DESIGN-003 (locked 2026-08-16). A project declares 1..N tracks in `.perry/config.md § Tracks`; each track has a mode, and the mode determines spine, item states, cadence driver, triage questions and default verification rung. Absent a Tracks section there is one implicit track named `main`, mode `project` — which is today's Perry exactly, so nothing here changes an existing project until it opts in.

queue.ends_when: never; steady state, reviewed on a period

inquiry.ends_when: the question is answered or abandoned

work_modes.defaults_note: Two different absences, and conflating them is a bug. `""` with the column listed in `no_default` means THERE IS NO HONEST DEFAULT and the track must declare it: `SLA` and `Cycle` are commitments a project makes to someone, and inventing one would put words in the user's mouth. `""` otherwise means THIS MODE HAS NO SUCH CONTROL - queue has no WIP cap by design (depth is reported, never enforced) and project mode has no stage vocabulary at all. A track missing a `no_default` column cannot run the triage step that reads it, and triage reports that as a finding rather than skipping silently (V4 re-review round 3, findings 6-7).

verification.note: DESIGN-003 section 5.3. Replaces the binary evidence gate with a declared rung per task. Advisory for one release (decision 4), then a hard gate. Two rules govern it, and neither is expressible as a column check: (1) the required rung is a function of CONSEQUENCE, not shape - anything outward-facing, irreversible, or carrying money/legal/safety exposure requires V5 minimum in every mode, overriding the mode default; (2) a V4 claim must cite an acceptance-criteria file and the reviewer must not have seen the reasoning that produced the artifact, or it is V1 wearing a costume.

rungs.V0: asserted - 'looks done'. Never valid. If the linter sees one, that is a finding, not a low rung.
rungs.V1: artifact exists - a file at a path. Attested by the agent.
rungs.V2: structural check - a linter over required sections / schema / format. Attested by a script.
rungs.V3: reproducible run - command + inputs + output, re-runnable. Attested by a script.
rungs.V4: rubric review - a fresh-context reviewer scores against written acceptance criteria. Attested by a second agent.
rungs.V5: human sign-off - name, date, and what they checked. Attested by the user.
rungs.V6: external confirmation - client accepted / filed / published / merged. Attested by the world.

i18n.description: Which text in a state file may be written in the project's document language (.perry/config.md § Document language) and which may not. Section headings and table column headers are localizable: every reader MUST accept the canonical English form and every alias listed here. Everything in `invariant` stays ASCII/English in every language, because it is matched, joined, or dereferenced by machines. Adding a language means adding its aliases here and widening the `match` regexes in `files[].headings` — nothing else in the schema changes. A language with no glossary block is still fully supported for prose; its documents keep the English headings.
invariant: file and directory names (BOARD.md, phase/, evidence/<YYYY-MM>/)
ID prefixes and ID bodies (REL-002, ADR-001, DESIGN-001, KR-O1.2, P-O1.2, USER-014)
enum values (not_started, in_progress, blocked, review, done, dropped, single, split, ...)
YAML frontmatter keys and values in phase/<NNN>-linkage.md
priority section names (P0, P1, P2) and architecture section markers (§1…§8)
dates (YYYY-MM-DD), ISO weeks (YYYY-WW), commit SHAs, file paths
command and subcommand names (/perry okr plan-phase)
header field names in .perry/config.md (the file that declares the language cannot be written in it)

stale_run_days.note: A pipeline whose stage is non-terminal for this long is reported as a stale run, so the interrupted-run card also nudges the user to retire it. A calibrated default, not a law - long enough that a genuinely paused adoption is not nagged, short enough to catch one that is actually dead. Declared here so perry-lint and the entry card read the same number.

claims.note: the anchor. Holds the State root pointer, so it can never sit behind it.
PMO scaffolds it; the user authors it. Mirrors files[id=architecture].owner.

optional_columns.Track: Which declared track this row belongs to. Absent = the implicit `main` track, mode `project`.
optional_columns.Verification: The verification rung this row must reach to close (DESIGN-003 section 5.3). Absent = the track's mode default. Validated only when the column is present, so no pre-DESIGN-003 board is invalidated.
optional_columns.Stage: For pipeline-, queue- and inquiry-mode rows: the item's position in its track's declared stage vocabulary. NOT enum-checked here, because the vocabulary is per-track (`.perry/config.md` Tracks -> Stages) rather than global - `Status` stays the global lifecycle enum and the two are orthogonal. Added by the V4 review of TASK-019/020 (finding B1): both mode files declared a stage vocabulary and neither said where a stage is written, so every rule that depended on stage position was uncomputable.
optional_columns.Arrived: The date an item entered the system from outside. Carried forward from `BOARD.md` Intake when a queue-mode row is routed, and REQUIRED to survive that move - V4 finding B2: age-since-arrival is what SLA triage measures, and destroying it at routing made the mode's second triage step uncomputable.
optional_columns.Commitment: The `Id` of the row in `OKR.md` Commitments that this row discharges - that id and nothing else. Never row position, never Promise text (V4 re-review finding N9).
optional_columns.Stage since: The date the row entered its current `Stage`. Mirrors `Arrived`, and exists for the same reason: dwell time is what pipeline triage measures first, and the journal records STATUS changes - so a `draft`->`review` move produces no journal line at all, because this design's own argument is that Status and Stage are orthogonal. V4 re-review finding N1: the Stage column closed B1 and left the clock with no source.
optional_columns.Parent: For inquiry-mode rows: the ID of the question this one was split out of. A question tree needs an edge, and BOARD.md has no nesting - so the edge is a cell. Absent = a root question. Written by add-task, read by triage to report which branches are still open.

tables.note: Untriaged external requests, for queue-mode tracks (DESIGN-003 decision 3). OPTIONAL: skipped entirely when the section is absent. Lives inside BOARD.md rather than a new INTAKE.md so the refactor claims no new path — BOARD.md is already in claims[]. `triage` drains this section as its first step. `Outcome` is required because triage mandates that every row be routed, dropped WITH A REASON, or deferred WITH A NAMED CONDITION - a table with nowhere to write the reason turns that rule into a suggestion. Empty cells are fine; the column is not.

optional_columns.Asked: YYYY-MM-DD the question was put to the user. Stamped by `perry-task ask`. This is what should be STORED; idle days are computed from it at read time.
optional_columns.Idle: Days the request has waited. DERIVED — a stored age is stale the moment it is written, which is why it is optional and why `Asked` exists. Read when present so no existing board breaks; never required.

tables.note: The recurrence register (DESIGN-003, `modes/queue.md` § Recurrence is a first-class object here). Written by `perry-task cadence-add` / `cadence-done`, read by `perry-state`, which reports rows past `Next due` by age. `Frequency` is NOT enum-checked: `weekly`, `monthly`, `quarterly` and `Nd` are what the tool writes, but `continuous` and `hourly` are live in a real project's register and mean a recurrence with no computable due date. Reading is tolerant and writing is strict — `perry-task` refuses a frequency it cannot schedule from; nothing rejects a cell a project already wrote. `Next due` is likewise free text: `n/a`, `2026-W32` and `**2026-08-31**（…）` are all live, and `bin/perry-state` reports the cells it could not read rather than treating them as never due.

optional_columns.Last run: YYYY-MM-DD the ritual last ran. Stamped by `perry-task cadence-done`. This is the INPUT `Next due` is computed from, and it exists so the due date can be CHECKED rather than trusted: without it, a `Next due` cell asserts a schedule with nothing on the board to derive it from, and an edited `Frequency` silently invalidates it with no way to tell. Same discipline as `Stage since`, `Arrived` and `Asked` — store the event's date, compute the derived value at read time. Absent on a row that has never run, which is not the same as a row that ran long ago.
optional_columns.Last evidence: Path to the artifact of the most recent run. Was REQUIRED until TASK-021, and a live register that keeps its evidence links inline in `Next due` carried a `table-columns` error for the whole time — a project penalized for a column it had a reason not to have, exactly as `Idle` was before TASK-039. `perry-task cadence-done` creates the column when it needs to write one, so requiring it up front bought nothing.

tables.note: Promises to a named party by a date - the spine for pipeline- and queue-mode tracks (DESIGN-003 section 5.5). OPTIONAL: skipped entirely when the section is absent, so no pre-DESIGN-003 OKR.md is invalidated. OWNED BY THE GOALS LANE, like every other section of this file: a commitment to a client is a goal, and DESIGN-003 already frames a KR as the special case where the party is the project itself. The modes disclaim the objectives->KRs cascade, not the goals file. V4 finding B4 is what forced the ownership to be stated: two modes were writing here and no lane had claimed it. `By when` is PER-MODE: a date for pipeline-track rows, which triage compares against; free prose for queue-track rows ('within the track SLA'), whose real clock is the register's `SLA`. One shared table, two formats - stated here because a pipeline triage that hits a queue row's prose would otherwise just stop (V4 re-review round 3, finding 4).

optional_columns.Discharged by: Free prose describing how the promise is satisfied. NOT a list of row IDs: the authoritative link runs the other way - each BOARD.md row's `Commitment` cell carries the `Id` from this table. Row position must never be used as the reference; the goals lane rewrites this file, and a position reference does not dangle when a row is inserted, it silently re-points every board row to the wrong promise (V4 re-review N9).

header_fields.name: Started
header_fields.note: phase day is computed from this

headings.match: ^Phase Scope Reduction Rule\b|^阶段缩圈规则|^缩圈规则
headings.label: ## Phase Scope Reduction Rule

headings.match: ^Not Doing in this phase\b|^本阶段不做
headings.label: ## Not Doing in this phase

frontmatter.description: The O→KR→task→agent graph. Machine-written by okr, machine-read by Perry (attribution) and by the frontend (the chain view). All-or-nothing: a half-parsed graph would show committed objectives as absent.

updated.note: full datetime; a day-only value is dropped, not guessed

target.note: NUMBER ONLY. Omit for prose targets ('<= 15% drawdown') — rendering a ceiling as completion is worse than rendering nothing.

tasks.note: BOARD task ids. This is the task->KR edge; a task listed here needs no inference.

unlinked.note: DECLARED, never inferred. Set arithmetic over the board would report the whole un-triaged backlog as drift.

projects.note: Perry's attribution registry. Extra key beyond the frontend's schema; the frontend ignores it.

frontmatter.description: The adoption dossier: everything /perry adopt inferred about an existing project, as candidates that have not touched the project. The ONLY file adoption writes before stage 4 — state files are written by their owning skills through the normal subcommands. Also the durable record of what was rejected, so --recheck does not re-propose it forever.

root.note: absolute path to the adopted project root

mode.note: merge = Perry state already exists; duplicates are surfaced to the user, never auto-dropped

stage.note: coarse position. Advanced only after the stage's writes are durable. `abandoned` is terminal and means the user retired the run; the dossier stays in place so its rejections remain the don't-ask-me-again record.

step.note: fine position WITHIN the stage. `confirm` and `commit` are each many ordered sub-steps, and resuming at the top of `confirm` re-runs the whole interview - the failure that caused the abandonment. Absent means the stage had not begun. See design DESIGN-001.

declarations.note: everything the USER authored or decided, persisted the instant it was said rather than at stage 4. `evidence proposes, the user declares` only holds within one session unless the declaration outlives it. `commit` writes FROM these, never from a re-render of candidates[].proposal.

step.note: which sub-step of confirm produced this

content.note: verbatim, multi-line. A KR carries id, statement, metric, target, baseline, stretch and deadline - candidates[].resolution is one line and cannot hold it.

materialized_as.note: the state file this declaration became at commit. Lets a partial commit be resumed without rewriting what already landed.

tier.note: caps the confidence of every candidate derived from this source

read.note: scan writes false; harvest flips it. The difference is what --resume needs.

name.note: named after the work, not the source

seed.note: roadmap_heading | commit_scope | module | issue_label | fs_timeline | misc — in preference order; see reference/adoption.md § Clustering

kr.note: result of the cluster->KR pass. Absent = not yet attributed. Every task in the cluster inherits this edge; it is DECLARED by the user, never matched by name.

confidence.note: Perry's reading of the evidence, NOT whether the candidate is a good idea

evidence.note: citations in the declared forms (path#Lx-y, git:sha, gh#id, fs:path@mtime). A candidate that cannot cite is dropped, not softened.

target.note: which state file it would land in, and therefore which skill writes it

status.note: rejected entries are KEPT — they are the don't-ask-me-again record

resolution.note: one line: why rejected / what the user edited it to

materialized_as.note: the real id it became at stage 4 (TASK-007, DESIGN-002, ADR-004)

frontmatter.description: The diagnosis record: how a project is structured for agent work, what was measured, what the user said, and what was prescribed. The ONLY file /perry diagnose writes. Works on any folder, Perry-adopted or not. Also the durable record of declined prescriptions, so --recheck does not re-propose them forever.

root.note: absolute path to the diagnosed project root

stage.note: coarse position. Advanced only after the stage's writes are durable. `abandoned` is terminal - a declined prescription stays in the doc rather than being re-proposed.

step.note: fine position WITHIN the stage. The interview is six questions and the execute stage is one item at a time; neither survives being restarted from the top. See design DESIGN-001.

scanned.note: what bin/perry-diagnose inferred from folder shapes; may be null, which is an honest answer

confirmed.note: what the user said. OVERRIDES scanned unconditionally.

maintenance_ceiling.note: the Q6 answer. A HARD CAP on the prescription, not a factor to weigh.

measurements.note: copied from the bin/perry-diagnose payload. Every number in the report comes from here; absent fields print '-' rather than being estimated.

restore_point.note: branch name or backup dir created before the first change. Stage execute may not begin while this is null.

id.note: stable id from bin/perry-diagnose (CTX/DOC/CON/TRK/FIT) or assigned for an interview finding

source.note: measured, or reported by the user. Nothing else may be a finding.

status.note: disputed is real - thresholds are calibrated defaults, not laws, and the user may reject one

change.note: one line - what actually changes on disk

closes.note: finding ids. An item that closes nothing does not belong on the list.

status.note: declined entries are KEPT - they are the don't-ask-me-again record

moves.note: every file relocation. This is what makes the run reversible by hand, so it is written as each move happens, not batched.

header_fields.name: Chat language
header_fields.note: language of the agent's conversational replies. Absent (or 'follow user') means mirror whatever language the user typed; a named language pins replies to it regardless. Written state files always follow `Document language`, never this field.

header_fields.name: State root
header_fields.note: relative path from the project root where Perry's state files live; default '.'. Set when the project already uses a directory Perry claims (design/ is the common collision). `.perry/` itself never moves — it is the anchor that holds this pointer.

header_fields.name: Packs
header_fields.note: Comma-separated pack names active in this project, resolved under $PERRY_HOME/packs/<name>/. Absent = software-ops only, which is what every pre-DESIGN-003 project effectively had. A pack supplies defaults - mode, stage vocabulary, rubrics, high-stakes additions, display glossary - never content.

tables.note: The track register (DESIGN-003 section 5.2). OPTIONAL: this spec is skipped entirely when the section is absent, which is what keeps every pre-DESIGN-003 project valid. Tracks are configuration, not state, which is why they live in a path Perry already claims rather than in a new file. Only Track and Mode are required; the rest are per-mode and absent columns take the mode default.

optional_columns.Spine: Free text: where this track's goals/commitments live.
optional_columns.Stages: Ordered stage vocabulary, arrow-separated, e.g. `brief->draft->review->approved->published`. Pipeline, queue and inquiry modes. Absent = the mode's default vocabulary. SEPARATOR: `->` is canonical. `→` (U+2192) is accepted and means the same thing; readers must normalize before splitting. Three spellings were in circulation and nothing normalized, so 'the first stage' and 'the terminal stage' were computed by splitting on a separator the corpus spelled three ways (V4 round 4, finding 11).
optional_columns.WIP: Per-stage limits, BY NAME ONLY: `stage:n`, comma-separated, e.g. `review:2,draft:4`. A stage not named has no limit. A positional grammar was considered and dropped - two grammars is one parser too many, and a user following the wrong one would produce a config that lints clean and evaluates to no limits at all. Pipeline default: `review:3`. Inquiry uses `open:n`, default `open:5`. Queue has no WIP control at all (depth is reported, never enforced), so the column is meaningless there.
optional_columns.SLA: The single home for turnaround expectations, for both pipeline dwell time and queue response time. V4 finding S7: the two mode files put SLA in two different places for modes the design expects to coexist in one project.
optional_columns.Cycle: What bounds the current horizon. Pipeline mode: a cycle boundary (`2026-W34`, `until 2026-09-30`, a campaign name). Queue mode: the review period, which reports rather than closes, and may be recurring (`monthly`, `quarterly`). V4 finding S6 created it for pipeline; re-review finding N8 widened it to the mode that also pointed at it. No default in any mode - see work_modes.defaults_note.

files.note: Digests of external sources. The provenance base for inquiry-mode tracks: a finding may cite `[SRC-n]`, and this entry is what guarantees the id exists, is unique, and carries an origin and a date. Added by TASK-023 - `knowledge/` was in claims[] but had no files[] entry, so nothing validated these headers at all.

header_fields.name: Id
header_fields.note: Stable citation id. Minted once at digest time and never reused, so a claim citing SRC-7 in a year still resolves to the same source.

cross_file.description: phase/CURRENT must name an existing phase file (or be absent / '(none)').
Each linkage row's Objective must match the Objective encoded in its Serves KR id (P-O1.2 -> O1).
Each linkage row's Serves KR should exist in the current phase file's KR set.
A design doc with Status: locked must have a non-empty Implementation plan.
A BOARD row at status done must carry an Evidence path.
.perry/hook.md should declare a high-stakes list; dispatch and autopilot match specs against it.
No two linkage projects may share a name or an alias — that ambiguity is exactly what the registry exists to prevent.
A task id may appear under at most one KR's tasks[]; two would make its attribution ambiguous.

packs.note: DESIGN-003 section 5.6 / 5.7. Packs live in $PERRY_HOME, NOT in the user's project, so they claim nothing and appear in no claims[] entry. `packs/<name>/pack.md` is the manifest.

sections.Glossary: Optional. A two-column table, `Term | Shown as`, that renames what Perry RENDERS. It is a third axis on the same mechanism as i18n: file names, IDs, enum values, column keys and command names stay invariant, and only the nouns a human reads change. A pack that renamed a file name would break every parser, which is why the glossary cannot reach them.

packs.invariant: Everything in i18n.invariant, plus: a glossary may never rename a schema column key, a heading the schema matches on, an enum value, or a path. It renames prose.
